Efficient Probing is simple, lightweight, and empirically compelling, with strong accuracy-parameter and accuracy-FLOP tradeoffs across several MIM backbones and downstream datasets.

The evaluation is fairly broad, covering multiple SSL paradigms, several datasets, low-shot and layer-wise settings, plus ablations for key design choices such as query count, value projection, attention dimension, and output dimension.
The localization/entropy analysis and attention visualizations add interpretability evidence and support the claim that EP learns complementary spatial attention patterns.
weaknesses: The core method is conceptually simple and close to existing attention-pooling, MIL, and slot/query-based aggregation ideas, so the novelty is moderate rather than major.
Many central results are presented mainly as crowded Pareto plots rather than exact tables with uncertainty; there are no reported variances, multiple seeds, or statistical tests.

Efficiency claims rely mostly on parameter counts and FLOPs beyond the frozen backbone; actual wall-clock speed, memory usage, and end-to-end evaluation cost are not sufficiently reported despite claims of speed-up.

The localization analysis is suggestive but not definitive: correlation between attention concentration and accuracy drop does not prove causal localization quality, and qualitative maps are limited.
Reproducibility is incomplete: implementation details are useful but code, exact per-method hyperparameters, FLOP formulas, and full numerical results are not clearly provided.

There are several presentation issues and minor inconsistencies, including typos in figure references and captions, overstrong language such as 'state-of-the-art' and 'spectacular gains,' and some hard-to-read plots.

strengths: The paper identifies a real evaluation issue for MIM-style visual representations: standard [CLS] or GAP linear probing can understate the usefulness of distributed patch tokens.
The proposed EP mechanism is simple and practically attractive, reducing attention pooling parameters and FLOPs while often preserving or improving probing accuracy.

The manuscript includes a reasonably broad empirical sweep across multiple datasets, MIM backbones, and other pretraining paradigms, plus useful ablations on query count, output dimension, and projection choices.
The unified framing of several attentive pooling/probing variants is helpful for organizing the design space.
weaknesses: The novelty is limited. EP is essentially learnable-query attention pooling with removed key/query projections, closely related to prior attentive MIL, slot/perceiver-style pooling, class-attention, and existing probing heads. The paper does not convincingly establish that this is a sufficiently new algorithmic contribution.

Several claims are overstated. The paper frames EP as a scalable alternative to fine-tuning and claims strong interpretability/localization, but evaluates almost entirely classification probing and does not show transfer to dense tasks, robustness, or actual replacement of fine-tuning in realistic settings.

The empirical evidence is broad but not rigorous enough: most main results are shown only in scatter plots, with few exact tables, no confidence intervals, no variance across seeds, and unclear statistical significance for often small gains over strong baselines.

Baseline fairness is under-specified. Many competitor heads are repurposed from different contexts, and the tuning protocol appears uneven, with learning-rate search for some settings but fixed learning rate for large datasets. It is unclear whether all baselines are comparably optimized under equal compute and parameter budgets.

The efficiency claim is incomplete. The manuscript reports FLOPs and parameter counts, but the headline speed-up is not backed by wall-clock training/inference time, memory measurements, or end-to-end cost across datasets and backbones.

The localization/interpretability analysis is weak. Attention mass inside bounding boxes and entropy are only indirect metrics; replacing a head with uniform attention is a confounded intervention; no causal or robustness evidence supports the stronger claims about avoiding shortcuts or improving interpretability.

Reproducibility is insufficient for a top-tier submission: implementation details for all heads and variants are sparse, code/checkpoints are not provided, and hyperparameters for baselines are difficult to reconstruct.

The writing is sometimes promotional and imprecise, with phrases such as “spectacular gains” and several figure/caption inconsistencies. This weakens confidence in the care of the experimental presentation.
